headline: Test 2: Virginia, 1640–1705 · 43:28

items.title: 43:28 · In their 2008 historical study White Cargo
items.detail: In their 2008 historical study White Cargo, Don Jordan and Michael Walsh document the scale and brutality of that early European servant pipeline.

items.title: 43:37 · Between 300 000 and 500 000 English
items.detail: Between 300,000 and 500,000 English, Scottish, and Irish men, women, and children were shipped to the American colonies under indenture across roughly a century and a half.

items.title: 43:48 · Mortality on the Atlantic crossing reached up
items.detail: Mortality on the Atlantic crossing reached up to thirty percent on severe voyages, and roughly forty percent of indentured arrivals died before completing their multi-year terms of Chesapeake field labor.

items.title: 44:00 · In a single year the London spirit-merchant
items.detail: In a single year, the London spirit-merchant William Thiene abducted 840 children from British streets for shipment to colonial plantations.

items.title: 44:08 · Court records preserve cases such as Elizabeth
items.detail: Court records preserve cases such as Elizabeth Abbott, an indentured servant beaten to death with five hundred lashes while the planter class shielded her master from capital punishment.
